title: Regulatory Spillovers and Data Governance: Evidence from the GDPR
authors: Christian Peukert; Stefan Bechtold; Michail Batikas; Tobias Kretschmer
eligible_reason: Not staggered. The GDPR effective date (after = date >= 25 May 2018) is common to all websites. Main specifications (Tables 4-5) regress log third-party requests/cookies on trend, after and post-trend interacted with the continuous EU-audience share (eu_audience, noneu_audience), with website FE (h) only and no calendar-time FE (interrupted time series with trend breaks); Table 6 interacts after with continuous policy-disclosure measures; Table 7 is an HHI time series; Tables 8-10 compare Google vs non-Google vendors with the same trend-break specification. No unit-specific adoption dates.
design_notes: Stata do/results.do (main text) and do/results_appendix.do. Website-day panel of EU/non-EU websites and vendor-level panels, 2018. reghdfe ... absorb(h) vce(cluster h) nocons. Appendix event study (ib21319.date##c.eu_audience) also uses the single GDPR date and a continuous exposure.

ineligible_specs_listed.reason: single common post date (GDPR); continuous EU-audience exposure; linear trend and post-trend terms; no time FE
continuous privacy-policy measures x after; trend terms
Google vs non-Google with trend breaks at the common GDPR date

data_files_note: Combined analysis datasets shipped (gdpr_website.dta 363 MB, gdpr_vendors.dta 252 MB); info.txt gives instructions to access the public raw data.
data_provenance_note: Authors' combined analysis data built from public web-crawl sources.
screener_notes: Screened from package and OpenAlex metadata (no article text). GDPR is a single-date policy; no staggered adoption.
